title: Orgwide Ambassador Roundup — Jan 12 2027
content:
Purpose: quick, human-readable roll-up of the Ambassador program highlights shared at today’s orgwide check-in. This is not the full deck — it’s the operational notes, open questions, and concrete follow-ups for engineering leads and the Ambassador cohort.

Attendees: Samira (host), Ethan, Marisol, Devon, + 18 Ambassadors from serving-runtime, observability, private-deployments, and console teams.

1) Weekly snapshot (what Ambassadors shared)
- Serving-runtime: initial latency experiment for prefix-caching on long-chat workloads — internal A/B shows 8–12% median tail improvement but 1–2% increase in token-cost due to missed batching opportunities. Need follow-up to tune batch windowing.
- Observability: prototype trace sampler that adds a 1-token trace header to heavy requests; reduced noise for tracing UI and saved ~20% storage on a 48hr window for sampled routes.
- Private-deployments: testing installer v0.9 on an air-gapped RHEL setup; installer logs surfaced two certificate-edge cases in customer's kubelet config. Working on small patch.
- Console: rollout experiment for per-route cost-breakdown is live for 10% of customers — UX feedback positive, noticed some confusion around which tokens are counted as “system” vs “user”.

2) Cross-team blockers flagged during the check-in
- Model-variant compatibility: Dedicated routing policies aren’t detecting quantized fallback model profiles consistently. Root-cause likely in model-metadata mapping logic when legacy model manifests are present. Action: Devon + serving-runtime to open a short spike (ENG-6129) and add unit tests for manifest edge-cases. Owner: Devon. ETA: 2027-01-24.
- Canary rollback speed: current rollback pipeline takes ~7 minutes because it waits for in-flight request drains; for high-SLA routes teams want <2m safe rollback. Action: platform-engineering + sre to prototype a graceful preemption signal to runtime. Owner: Marisol. ETA: 2027-02-02.

3) Outcomes we want to land before next Ambassador sync (Jan 19)
- Batch-window tuning knobs documented and a short playbook for app teams showing latency vs cost tradeoffs (owner: Ethan, content owner: Samira).
- Small patch for installer cert edge-cases landed on main and a test run reported (owner: Private-deployments eng lead).
- Add the manifest compatibility unit tests and a failing test case to prevent regressions (owner: Devon).

4) Decisions and policy updates
- Ambassadors voted (7–2) to prioritize predictable throughput for Dedicated over micro-optimizing token cost at 99.9% tail. Implication: default routing policy for Dedicated becomes conservative (prefer capacity-pinned quantized variants only when explicitly enabled). Policy doc updated: confluence:ENG-ambassador-policy-2027 (link in artifacts).
- Feature flag cadence: new rule — feature flags that touch routing/rollback must have a canary window of at least 48 hours when touching Dedicated routes.

5) Data & metrics highlights
- Latency experiment: median delta -9%, p95 delta -11% (serving-runtime prefix-cache A/B) but token-cost per request +1.8% for chat-legacy workloads.
- Observability trace sampling decreased ingest by ~20% over a rolling 48-hour window.
- Installer test failure rate for air-gapped builds dropped from 6% -> 1.2% after last infra-pr (small sample, n=85 runs).

6) Q&A highlights from the floor
- Q: Will we provide a fallback for routing when a quantized variant yields lower quality? A: Yes — roadmap item to attach a quality-score sentinel to model variants; if quality dips below threshold, traffic auto-fails back. Spike scheduled Q1.
- Q: Can Ambassadors get a curated list of low-cost evaluation prompts to compare quantized variants? A: Working list created — Samira to publish to the Ambassador Slack channel and Confluence.

7) Shoutouts / People
- Shoutout to observability engineers (Ana, Priya) for the quick prototype on trace headers.
- Thanks to the installer team (Liam, Nora) for pushing the air-gapped test infra.

8) Risks + unknowns (short risk register)
- Risk: if batch-window tuning prioritizes latency too much we could see a 3–5% increase in steady-state cost across heavy chat customers. Mitigation: create cost alarms per route with ±5% drift detection. Owner: Console product + Platform telemetry.
- Unknown: impact of upcoming GPU driver upgrade on quantized kernel performance. Action: schedule validation runs on the CI GPU fleet pre-upgrade. Owner: release-engineering.

9) Open action items (owners & due dates)
- Devon: spike + tests for manifest compatibility (ENG-6129). Due 2027-01-24.
- Ethan: batch-window playbook draft + example configs. Due 2027-01-19.
- Marisol: prototype graceful rollback preemption signal. Due 2027-02-02.
- Samira: publish Ambassador curated eval prompts and link to confluence. Due 2027-01-14.

10) Next sync format (Jan 19)
- 20-minute lightning updates from each vertical (serving-runtime, console, private, observability).
- 10-minute open floor for cross-team help requests.
- Quick poll at the end (what one thing would you want from platform next week?)

Notes to self (informal):
- Capture any emergent cross-team follow-ups and ping product PMs directly — avoid backlog surge on the Ambassador Slack channel.
- Consider creating a small ‘quick-win’ tag for action items that can be closed in <3 days so Ambassadors can get visible wins.

Raw links referenced in check-in:
- Spike ticket: JIRA ENG-6129 -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-6129
- Policy doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/ambassador-policy-2027
- Installer PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/installer/pull/341

Attachments: short CSV export of the experiment metrics table uploaded to the meeting thread.

If anything above is unclear or you want the raw notes from each ambassador, reply and I’ll paste the per-team snippets.
